intro: Professionals and everyday users convert gigabytes (GB) to terabytes (TB) when working across metric and metric standards in engineering specifications, international trade documentation, and technical measurements. One gigabyte (decimal) equals 0.001 terabytes, while 1 terabyte (decimal) equals 1,000 gigabytes. Whether you are verifying digital storage specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

faqs.question: How many terabytes (TB) are in 1 gigabyte (decimal) (GB)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.001 terabytes (TB) in 1 gigabyte (decimal) (GB), which rounds to 0.001 TB for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 terabyte (decimal) equals 1,000 gigabytes.

faqs.question: How do I convert gigabytes to terabytes (GB to TB)?
faqs.answer: To convert gigabytes to terabytes, use the formula: TB = GB × 0.001. For example, converting 16 GB gives 0.016 TB.

faqs.question: What is 16 gigabytes in terabytes?
faqs.answer: 16 gigabytes (GB) equals exactly 0.016 terabytes (TB) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
